issues.acceptance: Present the intact authored cemetery and Warden at readable gameplay scale with coherent moonlit exposure, landmark identity, collision agreement and high-angle composition comparable to the bound directional reference.

details.acceptance: Present the intact authored cemetery and Warden at readable gameplay scale with coherent moonlit exposure, landmark identity, collision agreement and high-angle composition comparable to the bound directional reference.
details.expected: The authored replacement fills the useful frame, exposes readable human-scale silhouettes and landmarks, and retains the reference's restrained warm-versus-cool hierarchy without visible rendering corruption.

measurements.expected: No runtime-visible mesh corruption findings on the accepted authored surface.
measurements.name: Runtime mesh validation
measurements.observed: 104 meshes checked; 73 degenerate-UV findings, including repeated cemetery fence/column surfaces and hostile-recipient meshes.

measurements.expected: Readable Warden silhouette, landmarks and authored arena density at 1280x720.
measurements.name: Spawn composition
measurements.observed: The arena is very dark and distant; the Warden reads mainly as a tiny lantern mark, with large unused dark-blue margins.

details.observed: The primitive builder was replaced with one intact authored cemetery package and authored Warden model, but the shipped integration remains underexposed and zoomed too far out. Movement magnifies empty background, and mesh validation reports widespread degenerate UVs on visible package surfaces.
reproduction: Boot at 1280x720 and inspect spawn.
Move east and north while the camera follows.
Compare silhouette scale, exposure and frame occupancy with the bound Mournlight reference; run visible-mesh validation.
retest_recipe: Keep the accepted authored packages intact and adjust only product-owned camera, outer datum, lighting/material integration and sight-lane layers.
Revalidate visible meshes and capture spawn, movement, dash and northeast route.
Confirm readable player scale, landmark exposure and useful arena occupancy without source-asset surgery.

task_specification.objective: Convert the preserved authored cemetery and combat foundation into a readable, populated, restartable survivor run, and replace the prototype gameplay overlay with a compact Mournlight HUD, while preserving the verified motor, dash, automatic-combat, weapon-build, package-integrity, and Godot boot baselines.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate remains a direct-to-active-play foundation rather than an integrated run. Scene-level camera values neutralize the intended occlusion profile, the intact cemetery lacks a cohesive product-owned framing/exposure/sight-lane wrapper, placed combat recipients substitute for spawned enemy lifecycles, and no authoritative controller owns title, failure, result, or clean retry. Separately, the gameplay HUD is an embedded collection of local text panels rather than a compact view of authoritative run state.

stop_conditions: Stop and report if native_godot_project or host_godot_boot regresses and the regression cannot be isolated within the selected candidate paths.

Do not edit, extract, duplicate, reposition, or replace children of the preserved cemetery, Frost Mage Warden, or lantern imports; stop if acceptance would require source-asset surgery or package replacement.
Do not weaken the verified planar motor, dash phases and ownership, deterministic targeting, attack causality, three weapon strategies, or exactly-once death/drop transactions.

Do not expand into upgrade drafting, the five-wave director, Bellkeeper implementation, broad animation rebinding, complete settings/accessibility, or audio qualification; those backlog surfaces remain outside this iteration.
Stop after the five selected gaps are closure-ready and leave the deferred animation issue unchanged.

strategy.rationale: Repair the world objective through wrapper and ownership changes rather than another isolated transform pass: centralize camera configuration, retain one intact authored environment, add validated enemy lifecycles, and make one run controller own entry, failure, result, and reset. Treat the HUD as a separate presentation family that consumes the resulting authoritative snapshots without owning gameplay.

done_when: Exactly one intact authored cemetery package remains the sole authoritative environment. Native paths, buildings, graves, vegetation, props, materials, and landmarks supply the visible composition; only an outer datum, collision, spawn/objective anchors, gameplay boundaries, lighting, and camera-aware sight-line support are added outside the import.

Camera configuration has one explicit owner. Repeating the ordinary D-then-W northeast route to approximately (15.23, 0.05, -9.11) keeps the complete Warden silhouette, nearby collision context, a threat, and at least one escape direction visible without exposing a large empty blue background.

At 1280x720, spawn, movement, dash, northeast-route, and useful landmark views show readable human-scale silhouettes, useful cemetery occupancy, moonlit blue-violet ambient fill, warm Warden light, distinct hostile accents, restrained fog/glow, and no visible primitive stand-ins, proxy floor, floating props, material failure, or rendering corruption.

The four ordinary PRD roles are data-driven over bounded shared contracts: Mossling supplies durable melee pursuit, Wispbat readable flank pressure, Bone Slinger wind-up/projectile/recovery, and Grave Brute a telegraphed slam and body-block threat. This task does not implement the Bellkeeper or five-wave director.

A deterministic encounter spawner rejects positions inside the protected camera region, inside collision, outside the playable datum, within the minimum player-safe radius, or without a valid approach. Spawned enemies enter through readable lanes and cannot inflict first-frame surprise damage.

Each ordinary role completes spawn, approach/separation, attack telegraph, damage frame, hurt, exactly-once death/drop, and pool return. Following one stable enemy id through reuse proves health, target, velocity, timers, visibility, collision, animation state, pending work, and signal ownership reset.

Enemy separation avoids violent jitter, permanent clumps, and unavoidable body locking. Contact, projectile, and slam damage remain separately cued and bounded, and ordinary pressure preserves a recoverable movement choice.

One authoritative run controller owns title, initializing, active, paused, failure, result, retrying, and return-to-title states. The configured build starts on Title, reaches gameplay through ordinary UI input, enters failure exactly once from ordinary enemy damage, and reaches Result without restarting the application.
